item.title: The Assembly of Lovers - Sufi Drum Circle — Mon Aug 17, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description: Community drum and chant circle rooted in Sufi prayer. Contribution: Sliding scale donation $20–$40 (no one will be turned away) This is a vibrant Community Drum and Chanting Circle, where we drum and chant from our hearts into the universe. This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound. The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy. You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer. It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. There is a rhythm older than thought. A pulse that moves beneath language, beneath belief, beneath the self that thinks it’s separate. The Mystics knew this. The Sufis practiced it in Majalis al-‘Ushshāq. The Assembly of Lovers. Not

item.title: Going Global: A Free Two-Part Workshop Series — Tue Aug 18, 12:00 PM — Online
item.description:
Ready to take your business beyond U.S. borders? Join us for a FREE two-part workshop series designed to transform your growth from local to worldwide. On August 4, we'll explore whether exporting is the right move for your business, assess your readiness, and identify which of your products or services have international demand. By August 18, you'll be ready for part two, where we'll dive into the real logistics—finding international buyers, navigating permits and paperwork, and mapping out your clear path forward. Expert facilitator Reina Valenzuela will guide you through the opportunities, close your knowledge gaps, and leave you with a concrete action plan. Whether you're curious about global expansion or ready to take the leap, this free series gives you the framework and clarity to do it right.
Hosted by: Feliciano Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation

item.title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio — Tue Aug 18, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and draw. Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. item.description: FABRIC is a welcoming arts and wellness series designed for adults 55+ to foster creativity, connection, and well-being. item.description: What if you could bottle up the very beginning of your Montclair story? Montclair Mixtape is a collaborative Welcome Week zine where every student gets to create a page that captures who they are right now—their favorite songs, big goals, random interests, and everything they hope to experience during their first year at Montclair. Then, make it yours! Decorate your page with stickers, doodles, magazine cutouts, colors, lyrics, photos, or anything else that feels like you. 1\. No instruction or orders are allowed on any of our group courts\. Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and draw. Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. item.description: The Space for Words – literary open-mic night hosted by the NJ Poetry Circle August 28 | Doors open at 7:30, start time 8 pm | $10 for everyone This is a monthly event on the last Friday of every month, holidays permitting. Hey writers, poets, and storytellers! Come share your art with us at The Space for Words Open Mic Night. Whether you’re a seasoned author or just getting started, this is your chance to share your work in front of a supportive and inspiring audience. Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work — the stage is yours! The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Each performer gets a maximum of 5 minutes to read, and at the end we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. Come for the words, stay for the community. item.title: Eagle Rock Hike — Sat Aug 29, 10:00 AM — Meet at Student Recreation Center
item.description:
Take a gentle hike at Eagle Rock Reservation to a striking view of Manhattan. A thoughtful way to observe and remember September 11, 2001. The trip departs from the Student Recreation Center. How do I Sign-up?
Register here or in the Student Rec Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). Cost for Students $10
Where and When?
Saturday the 29th, 2026 10am-2pm Begins Student Recreation Center
What to bring: Water, Lunch, Boots or Sneakers, and Sunscreen. Potential Hazards: unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, dehydration, allergic reactions/poisonous plants, insect bites, injury by running including sprains, lacerations, abrasions and fractures.
Hosted by: Campus Recreation
Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12520013
Source: Montclair State University
